auditor_value: None of the above (T(A) = 98 N, T(B) = 98/cos30° ≈ 113.2 N, T(C) = T(B) sin30° ≈ 56.6 N with g = 9.8; all non-zero)

findings.note: String B makes 30° with the VERTICAL (question text and figure both say so), so its vertical component is T(B) cos30°, not T(B) sin30°. This is the wrong formula for the served geometry; a student who copies it loses the mark on any numeric version of this problem.
The horizontal component of a string at 30° to the vertical is T(B) sin30°, not T(B) cos30°. With the correct T(B) ≈ 113.2 N this gives T(C) ≈ 56.6 N, not 169.7 N.
Follows from the swapped component in step 1. The correct value is T(B) = 98 / cos30° = 98 / 0.866 ≈ 113.2 N.
Two of the three listed tensions are wrong (consequence of the swapped sin/cos). The conclusion that none is zero still holds with the correct values.
